hostName.title: Computer Name
hostName.summary: How this computer shows up on your network
hostName.text: The name other devices on your network see. Left empty, it's the name of this computer's folder in machines/. Use letters, numbers and hyphens.

windowManager.summary: The desktop everyone on this computer logs in to
windowManager.text: The window manager for everyone on this computer. **niri** lays windows out in columns on a strip you scroll through, with **DankMaterialShell** for the bar, launcher and lock screen.

kernel.summary: The Linux kernel this computer starts
kernel.text: **Zen** and **XanMod** are tuned for desktops and games; setup.sh picks Zen. **Latest** is the newest stable kernel. **CachyOS** compiles on this computer, which !!takes a long time!!, and needs a CPU with AVX2 (x86-64-v3).

cursor.title: Pointer Theme
cursor.summary: The mouse pointer, login screen included
cursor.text: **Bibata Modern Ice** in white, or **Catppuccin** Mocha Mauve to match the desktop. Open apps switch when you restart them.

cursorSize.title: Pointer Size
cursorSize.text: The pointer size before screen scaling. A size picked in DankMaterialShell's settings goes back to this one on the next rebuild.

timeZone.title: Time Zone
timeZone.summary: Sets the clock for everyone on this computer
timeZone.text: The time zone the clock, logs and file times use. setup.sh copies it from the NixOS installer.

locale.title: Language & Formats
locale.summary: Programs' language, and how dates, numbers and money look
locale.text: The language programs use when they have a translation, and how dates, times, numbers, paper sizes and money are written. The Japanese locale is installed too, for games that need it.

keyboardLayout.title: Keyboard Layout
keyboardLayout.summary: The layout on the desktop and the login screen
keyboardLayout.text: The disk password prompt uses Console Keymap below instead. To switch between several layouts, add them on the shell's Keyboard page.

consoleKeyMap.title: Console Keymap
consoleKeyMap.summary: The layout before the desktop starts
consoleKeyMap.text: The layout for the disk password prompt at boot and the text consoles (Ctrl+Alt+F2 and on). Match it to the desktop layout; a few have other names here, such as "uk" for "gb".

capsLockRemap.title: Caps Lock as Escape and Ctrl
capsLockRemap.summary: Escape when tapped, Ctrl when held
capsLockRemap.text: Works on every keyboard, through **keyd**. Turn it off for a normal Caps Lock.

bluetooth.enable.title: Bluetooth
bluetooth.enable.summary: Headphones, controllers and other wireless devices
bluetooth.enable.text: Turns on the Bluetooth adapter and powers it up at boot. Pair devices from the Bluetooth panel in the shell's control center.

printing.enable.title: Printing
printing.enable.summary: Print to USB and network printers
printing.enable.text: **CUPS** prints, and **Avahi** finds network printers that need no driver (it opens UDP port 5353). Add printers on the shell's Printers page, below once this is on.

firewall.openTCPPorts.title: Open TCP Ports
firewall.openTCPPorts.summary: For a game or web server others connect to
firewall.openTCPPorts.text: Ports other devices may connect to over TCP; every other port stays closed. SSH, Syncthing, Sunshine, Steam and printing open their own, so they don't go here.

firewall.openUDPPorts.title: Open UDP Ports
firewall.openUDPPorts.summary: Some game and voice servers need these too
firewall.openUDPPorts.text: Port numbers other devices may send UDP traffic to. Game servers often want the same number open for both TCP and UDP.

blocklist.enable.title: Block Ads and Trackers
blocklist.enable.summary: A hosts list blocks them for every app at once
blocklist.enable.text: **Steven Black's hosts list** blocks known ad, tracker and malware domains. If a site or app breaks, turn this off to check whether it's the cause.

blocklist.extra.title: Also Block
blocklist.extra.summary: Extra lists on top of ads and trackers
blocklist.extra.text: Extra lists from the same project. Social networks covers sites such as Facebook, Instagram and TikTok, so turn it on only if you don't use them on this computer.

mullvad.enable.title: Mullvad VPN
mullvad.enable.text: **Mullvad VPN** over WireGuard, with multihop and DAITA. A kill switch blocks all traffic while the tunnel is down.

mullvad.splitTunnel.title: Apps Outside the VPN
mullvad.splitTunnel.text: Apps switched on here always go around the VPN and use your normal connection, for games and services that block VPN addresses.

ssh.enable.title: SSH Server
ssh.enable.summary: Log in to this computer from another device
ssh.enable.note: !!Add your public key under Account first!!
ssh.enable.text: Key login only: no passwords and no root login. **fail2ban** bans an address for 12 hours after 3 failed attempts. !!Without a key under Account, there's no way in.!!

clamav.enable.title: ClamAV Virus Scanner
clamav.enable.summary: Background virus scanning, plus a window to scan files
clamav.enable.note: !!Uses about 1 GB of RAM even when idle!!
clamav.enable.text: **ClamAV** antivirus: a background scanner, automatic definition updates, and the **ClamTK** window for scanning files by hand.

docker.enable.title: Docker
docker.enable.text: **Docker** and **Docker Compose** for running containers. Admins join the docker group.

suwayomi.enable.title: Suwayomi Manga Server
suwayomi.enable.summary: A manga reader with a web page
suwayomi.enable.note: Opens in Helium, so turn Helium on too
suwayomi.enable.text: A local manga reader at localhost:4567, using the same extensions as Mihon. Its launcher opens it in **Helium** after a password prompt.

syncthing.enable.title: Syncthing
syncthing.enable.summary: Keep folders in sync between your devices
syncthing.enable.text: **Syncthing** keeps folders in sync between your devices directly, peer to peer. Runs as the main user; its settings page is at 127.0.0.1:8384.

flatpak.enable.title: Flatpak
flatpak.enable.summary: Sandboxed apps from Flathub or a downloaded bundle, with Flatseal
flatpak.enable.text: For apps nixpkgs doesn't have, like the Hytale launcher. **Flatseal** sets which folders, devices and network each app may reach. Turning this off keeps installed apps on disk, but they won't start until it's back on.

sunshine.enable.title: Sunshine Game Streaming
sunshine.enable.summary: Stream games to Moonlight on other devices
sunshine.enable.text: **Sunshine** streams games from this computer to **Moonlight** apps on other devices on your home network. Its settings page is at https://localhost:47990.

git.name.title: Name
git.name.text: The author name git puts on your commits. Left empty, git uses your login name.

git.email.title: Email
git.email.text: The email git puts on your commits. A GitHub no-reply address keeps your real one out of public repositories.

ssh.authorizedKeys.title: SSH Keys
ssh.authorizedKeys.summary: Public keys that may log in as you
ssh.authorizedKeys.text: Public keys allowed to log in over SSH on a computer with the SSH server on. A public key isn't a secret, so it's safe in the repo.

defaultApps.browser.title: Web Browser
defaultApps.browser.text: With **FreeTube** on, YouTube links go there instead. If the browser picked here is switched off, the first one that's on is used.

defaultApps.textEditor.title: Text Editor
defaultApps.textEditor.text: If the editor picked here is switched off, the first one that's on is used.

defaultApps.terminal.title: Terminal
defaultApps.terminal.summary: Runs terminal programs from the launcher
defaultApps.terminal.text: Also used by file managers. If the terminal picked here is switched off, the first one that's on is used.

defaultApps.fileManager.title: File Manager
defaultApps.fileManager.text: If the file manager picked here is switched off, the first one that's on is used.

wallpaper.title: Wallpaper Source
wallpaper.summary: Still images, or animated Wallpaper Engine scenes
wallpaper.note: Engine !!needs Wallpaper Engine bought on Steam!!
wallpaper.text: **Still images** come from the repo's wallpaper folder. **Wallpaper Engine** plays animated scenes and videos from the Steam Workshop, and !!needs Wallpaper Engine bought on Steam.!! Mod+W opens the picker either way.

browsers.zen.text: **Zen** browser, set up with the **Arkenfox** and **Securefox** privacy tweaks.

browsers.mullvad.summary: Privacy browser from Mullvad and the Tor Project
browsers.mullvad.text: **Mullvad Browser**, made by the Tor Project and Mullvad to make its users hard for trackers to tell apart, without Tor's network. Works with or without a VPN.

browsers.helium.summary: Browser that also opens the Syncthing and Suwayomi pages
browsers.helium.text: **Helium** browser. It also opens the Syncthing and Suwayomi pages as app windows.

browsers.ferdium.text: All your web messengers in one window with **Ferdium**; you pick the services inside the app.

terminals.kitty.summary: Fast terminal drawn on the GPU
terminals.kitty.text: **Kitty** terminal. The file manager's "open in terminal" entry opens Kitty.

terminals.ghostty.text: **Ghostty**, a terminal themed like the rest of the desktop. Pick which terminal runs terminal programs under Default Apps.

editors.helix.text: **Helix**, a modal editor in the terminal: select text first, then act on it. Space opens its command menu and ? shows the keys. New to it? Run hx --tutor. This config adds Space w to save, Space q to quit and jk to leave insert mode.

editors.zed.summary: Code editor with language servers ready
editors.zed.text: **Zed**, a code editor, with language servers for Nix, Rust, TypeScript, Lua, YAML and Markdown installed beside it.

fileBrowsers.nautilus.text: **Nautilus**, the regular file manager window, with an Open in Kitty entry in its right-click menu.

fileBrowsers.dolphin.text: **Dolphin**, KDE's file manager, themed to match the GTK apps.

fileBrowsers.yazi.text: **Yazi**, a file manager that runs inside the terminal.

fileBrowsers.duxFiles.text: **Dux Files**, a standalone file manager from Dux Labs with tabs, split view, column view and archive support.

media.mpv.text: **mpv**, the video player. The Twitch browser and Moku play their videos in it.

media.freetube.text: Watch YouTube without an account in **FreeTube**; subscriptions stay on your computer, and YouTube links from other apps open in it. Left open during Apply, it overwrites its new settings when it exits.

media.videoTrimmer.summary: Cut a clip out of a video
media.videoTrimmer.text: Cut a clip out of a video without re-encoding it.

media.constrict.summary: Shrink a video to a file size
media.constrict.text: Re-encode a video so it fits a file size you choose.

media.moku.text: **Moku** reads manga, light novels and anime, with a button that opens the current episode in mpv.

media.streamlinkTwitchGui.summary: Browse Twitch and watch in mpv
media.streamlinkTwitchGui.text: Browse **Twitch** and watch streams in mpv, with no ads and no Twitch account; your follow list stays on this computer.

media.boorusama.text: Browse booru image sites with **Boorusama**. Its data sits in an encrypted vault that the launcher unlocks with a password and locks again on exit.

media.tonkatsuBox.summary: Track games, films, anime, books and music
media.tonkatsuBox.text: Track games, films, anime, manga, books and music in one local database with **Tonkatsu Box**, with imports from Steam and AniList. Setup: docs/personal/local/local-binary-installs.md.

graphics.krita.text: **Krita** for digital painting and drawing, with the **G'MIC** filters plugin.

graphics.affinity.summary: Photo, Designer and Publisher, through Wine

artcraft.photocraft.title: PhotoCraft
artcraft.photocraft.text: **PhotoCraft**, a layered photo editor that opens and saves PSD files.

artcraft.lightcraft.title: LightCraft
artcraft.lightcraft.text: **LightCraft**, a non-destructive editor for RAW photos.

artcraft.vectorcraft.title: VectorCraft
artcraft.vectorcraft.text: **VectorCraft**, a vector art and SVG editor.

artcraft.designcraft.title: DesignCraft
artcraft.designcraft.text: **DesignCraft**, a page layout and print design editor.

artcraft.figcraft.title: FigCraft
artcraft.figcraft.text: **FigCraft**, for designing and prototyping app interfaces.

artcraft.effectcraft.title: EffectCraft
artcraft.effectcraft.text: **EffectCraft**, a motion graphics and compositing tool.

artcraft.wordcraft.title: WordCraft
artcraft.wordcraft.text: **WordCraft**, a word processor that opens Word documents.

artcraft.gridcraft.title: GridCraft
artcraft.gridcraft.text: **GridCraft**, a spreadsheet that opens Excel files.

audio.reaper.text: **REAPER**, a program for recording and mixing (a DAW), with the **SWS** and **ReaPack** extensions.

audio.guitarix.text: **Guitarix**, a guitar amp simulator built as a chain of effects. Any guitar app also adds shared cabinet IRs, a tuner and **qpwgraph** for routing audio.

audio.tone3000.summary: Amp captures and IRs from TONE3000
audio.tone3000.text: The official **NAM** player; browse and load amp captures and IRs from the **TONE3000** library inside the app.

audio.katanaFloorboard.summary: Patch editor for a BOSS Katana MkII
audio.katanaFloorboard.text: Edit the patches on a **BOSS Katana MkII** amp from your computer. Setup: docs/personal/local/local-binary-installs.md.

office.obsidian.text: **Obsidian** keeps your notes as Markdown files in folders called vaults.

office.homebank.text: **HomeBank** personal accounting: label your transactions and see a running balance.

security.bleachbit.text: **BleachBit** clears caches, logs and browser leftovers when you run it; nothing runs on a schedule.

security.keepassxc.text: **KeePassXC**, an offline password manager. Its vault file can be synced between devices with **Syncthing**.

system.resources.text: **Resources**, a system and process monitor: what's running and how much it uses.

scrcpy.enable.title: scrcpy
scrcpy.enable.summary: Show and control an Android device
scrcpy.enable.text: Show and control an **Android** phone or tablet from your computer, over USB or wifi. Nothing gets installed on the device.

gaming.steam.note: Installed for everyone on this computer
gaming.steam.text: **Steam**, for running Windows games through Proton.

gaming.prismlauncher.text: **Prism Launcher** keeps separate Minecraft installs, each with its own game version and mods.

gaming.lutris.text: **Lutris** installs and runs games through Wine and emulators, with **Winetricks**, **cabextract** and **7-Zip** for installers that need them.

gaming.faugus.text: **Faugus Launcher** runs Windows games through **UMU** and Proton, the compatibility layer Steam uses, without Steam.

gaming.twintail.text: **Twintail Launcher** installs, updates and runs gacha games on Linux.

gaming.easyrpg.text: Plays **RPG Maker 2000/2003** games, plus a **Tobira no Densetsu** launcher upscaled in gamescope.

gaming.xsystem4.text: **xsystem4** runs games made with the System 4 engine natively, without Wine. Start it with xsystem4 followed by the game's folder.

gaming.feedback.text: **feedBack**, a guitar rhythm game that plays **Guitar Pro** tabs with your guitar as the input, through its own audio engine with VST plugins and amp models.

gaming.rocksmith.summary: Rocksmith 2014 with a BOSS Katana as the input
gaming.rocksmith.note: !!A few install steps are done by hand!!
gaming.rocksmith.text: Sets up **Rocksmith 2014** on Steam (Proton) to read your guitar through a **BOSS Katana**. Steps: docs/personal/gaming/rocksmith-2014.md.

gaming.r2modman.text: **r2modman** installs and manages mods from **Thunderstore**, for games such as Risk of Rain 2.

gaming.pathOfBuilding.text: **Path of Building** for both Path of Exile games, through **Rusty PoB**.

gaming.ludusavi.text: **Ludusavi** backs up your game saves every day to ~/SyncBackups/<computer>/Ludusavi.

gaming.retroshelf.summary: Tidies an ES-DE / RetroDECK game library
gaming.retroshelf.text: **RetroShelf** helps prune an ES-DE / RetroDECK roms folder, fills in metadata and artwork, renames files and imports games. New versions come with each flake update.

gaming.granblueRelinkMods.summary: Mod tools for Granblue Fantasy: Relink
gaming.granblueRelinkMods.text: **RelinkModOrganizer** for data mods and **Reloaded-II** for code mods, for Granblue Fantasy: Relink.

discord.vesktop.summary: Discord with Vencord, in the desktop's colours
discord.vesktop.note: !!Slow first build!! (built with its own Vencord)
discord.vesktop.text: **Discord** with **Vencord** built in, through Vesktop. Its colours follow the desktop theme live.

discord.arrpc.enable.summary: Show what you're playing on Discord
discord.arrpc.enable.text: Shows the Steam or Proton game you're playing on your **Discord** profile, through GoofCord or Vesktop.

claude.enable.summary: Anthropic's coding agent for the terminal
claude.enable.text: **Claude Code**, Anthropic's coding agent for the terminal, set up with this repo's skills, subagents and MCP servers.

localAi.code.title: Coding Models
localAi.code.summary: The models opencode and Zed can use
localAi.code.note: !!Download each one in LM Studio first!!

choices.ornith-1.5-35b-a3b: Ornith 1.5 35B A3B — MoE tuned for coding agents, 128K context, ~36 tok/s, most reliable in testing (recommended)
choices.qwen3.6-35b-a3b-q4: Qwen3.6 35B A3B (Q4) — MoE, 128K context, ~38 tok/s, finishes faster on short tasks

localAi.code.text:
Turn on the models you want in **opencode** and **Zed**'s agent panel. llama-swap loads the one you pick, one at a time. The first one turned on is the default, and each also gets a **fast** version with thinking off.

To download one, search LM Studio's Discover tab for its repo and download the named file:
• **Ornith 1.5 35B A3B**: ornith-ai/Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-GGUF, the Q4_K_M file (~23 GB)
• **Qwen3.6 35B A3B (Q4)**: unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF, the UD-Q4_K_XL file (~21 GB)

!!Without the file, opencode and Zed get an error the first time they use the model.!!

localAi.edit.title: Inline Suggestions

choices.sweep-next-edit-1.5b: Sweep Next-Edit 1.5B — predicts your next edit (recommended)
choices.qwen2.5-coder-1.5b: Qwen2.5 Coder 1.5B — completes the code at the cursor

localAi.edit.text:
The small model behind **Zed**'s inline suggestions (Tab accepts one). It runs on the CPU, so the coding model keeps the GPU. **Sweep** suggests edits anywhere near the cursor; **Qwen2.5 Coder** only fills in at the cursor.

To download one, search LM Studio's Discover tab for its repo:
• **Sweep Next-Edit 1.5B**: sweepai/sweep-next-edit-1.5B
• **Qwen2.5 Coder 1.5B**: ggml-org/Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Q8_0-GGUF

localAi.chat.title: Chat Models
localAi.chat.note: !!Download each one in LM Studio first!!

choices.gemma-4-26b-a4b: Gemma 4 26B A4B — Google's MoE, natural writing

localAi.chat.text:
Turn on the models you want for conversation. They share the GPU with the coding models, so llama-swap loads one at a time and the first message after a switch waits for it. Chat in **Open WebUI** (turn it on under Tools) or **llama-swap's Playground** (http://127.0.0.1:8090). Each one except Gemma also gets a **fast** version.

To download one, search LM Studio's Discover tab for its repo and download the named file:
• **gpt-oss 20B**: ggml-org/gpt-oss-20b-GGUF (~13 GB)
• **Gemma 4 26B A4B**: unsloth/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-qat-GGUF, the UD-Q4_K_XL file (~14 GB)

opencode.enable.summary: Open-source coding agent for the terminal
opencode.enable.text: **opencode**, an open-source coding agent for the terminal that works with many model providers, local ones included. Sharing chats to opencode.ai is turned off.

lmstudio.enable.summary: Run language models on this computer
lmstudio.enable.text: **LM Studio** downloads open language models and runs them on this computer, with a chat window and a local server other apps can talk to.

japanese.ime.title: Japanese Typing
japanese.ime.text: Type Japanese (hiragana, katakana and kanji) with **fcitx5** and **Mozc**.

japanese.vn.title: Japanese Visual Novel Tools
japanese.vn.summary: Run raw Japanese games and unpack their files
japanese.vn.text: Tools for raw Japanese visual novels: a launcher that runs games in a Japanese locale, and **innoextract**, **cabextract** and **mdf2iso** for unpacking them.
